modules.title: 1. Python Basics & Syntax
modules.description: Learn syntax, output with print(), numbers, and comments in Python.

lessons.title: The print() Function
lessons.summary: The print() function outputs text or numbers onto your screen. Learn its syntax and quote rules.
learningObjectives: Understand how print() displays data to the screen
Learn how quotation marks define text strings
Write and run your first Python program

sections.title: What is the print() Function?
sections.content: The `print()` function is used to output text or data onto your screen. It is one of the most frequently used functions in Python.

components.purpose: The built-in instruction telling Python to display something.
Parentheses that hold the data (arguments) you want to display.
Quotation marks telling Python that the text inside is a string literal.

terms.definition: A set of ordered instructions written in code for a computer to execute.
terms.example: A script that prints a greeting.

terms.definition: A sequence of text characters enclosed inside quotation marks.

sections.title: Try it Yourself
sections.instructions: Change the text inside the quotes to 'Welcome to Python!' and click Run Code.
hints: Keep the quotation marks around your new text.
Replace Hello, World! with Welcome to Python!

questions.question: Insert the missing keyword to output text on screen: ____("Hello, World!")
questions.prompt: Insert the missing keyword to output text on screen: ____("Hello, World!")
questions.hint: It is the function you just used to display text.
questions.explanation: The print() function outputs text or data to the console.

mistakes.title: Capitalizing Print
mistakes.explanation: Python is case-sensitive! Built-in functions must be lowercase.

mistakes.title: Missing closing quote
mistakes.explanation: Every opening quotation mark requires a matching closing quotation mark.

sections.title: Lesson Recap
takeaways: The print() function displays data to the screen.
Text strings must be enclosed in matching quotes.
Python executes instructions line by line from top to bottom.
